headline: Brazil's Ibovespa drops 2.7% as long-term interest rates spike on fiscal worries
summary: The Ibovespa index fell 2.68% to 171,006 points while long-term DI interest rates rose. Investors cited heightened fiscal and political caution following the presidential election runoff.
why: Brazilian equity and interest rate markets reflect sovereign fiscal health, foreign portfolio flows, and domestic inflation expectations.

impacts.name: Brazilian Equities
impacts.why: Rising domestic interest rates and fiscal concerns pressured equity valuations across Brazil.

why_moved: Concerns over Brazil's fiscal trajectory and political environment pushed domestic interest rate futures higher and depressed equity prices.
